question: Identify the vector quantity among these listed physical quantities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gravitational Intensity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction and follows the laws of vector addition. Gravitational intensity (also called gravitational field strength, defined as force per unit mass, g = F/m) has a definite direction — towards the centre of the attracting body — so it is a vector. (गुरुत्वीय तीव्रता — सदिश राशि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Energy, Mass and Density are scalar quantities — they are fully described by magnitude alone and have no direction.

• Other common scalars: distance, speed, time, temperature, work, power, volume, pressure, electric charge, electric potential.

• Other common vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, weight, momentum, impulse, torque, electric field, magnetic field.

NOTE

• Unit of gravitational intensity: N/kg (equivalent to m/s²). At the Earth's surface its value is about 9.8 N/kg.

• Remember: weight (mg) is a vector, but mass is a scalar; velocity is a vector, but speed is a scalar.

question: ‘The Palace of Illusions’, a rendition of the Hindu epic ‘Mahabharata’, was written by which of the following novelists?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Palace of Illusions" (2008) was written by the Indian-American author Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni. It retells the Mahabharata from the point of view of Draupadi (Panchaali). (द पैलेस ऑफ इल्यूजन्स — चित्रा बनर्जी दिवाकरुनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Her other well-known works include The Mistress of Spices, Sister of My Heart, The Forest of Enchantments (the Ramayana told by Sita) and The Last Queen (on Rani Jindan).

• Pratibha Ray is the Odia writer of "Yajnaseni", another acclaimed Draupadi-centred novel; she won the Jnanpith Award (2011).

• Indu Sundaresan wrote "The Twentieth Wife" (on Nur Jahan) and Devi Yesodharan wrote "Empire".

NOTE

• Other modern retellings of the epics: The Palace of Illusions (Divakaruni), The Great Indian Novel (Shashi Tharoor), Jaya (Devdutt Pattanaik), Ajaya and Asura (Anand Neelakantan).

question: G Krishnakumar was appointed chairman of which of the following in 2023?
option_1: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• G Krishnakumar was appointed Chairman and Managing Director of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) in 2023. (भारत पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• BPCL is a Maharatna public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, headquartered in Mumbai. It operates refineries at Mumbai, Kochi and Bina.

• ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) is India's largest crude oil and natural gas producer, headquartered in New Delhi.

• IOCL (Indian Oil Corporation Ltd) is the country's largest oil refining and marketing company, headquartered in New Delhi.

• HPCL (Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd) is headquartered in Mumbai and is a subsidiary of ONGC.

NOTE

• India's Maharatna oil PSUs include IOCL, ONGC, BPCL, HPCL and GAIL. The Maharatna status gives them greater autonomy in investment decisions.

question: ______________ was the first Indian woman to write an autobiography and also the first to do so in Bengali in her book titled ‘Aamar Jiban’, which was published in 1876.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rassundari Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rassundari Devi (1809–1899) was the first Indian woman to write a full-length autobiography, and the first to do so in Bengali. Her book "Aamar Jiban" ("My Life") was published in 1876. (आमार जीबन — राससुंदरी देवी)

• She taught herself to read and write secretly, at a time when literacy was forbidden to housewives in orthodox Bengali households.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sarala Devi Chaudhurani was a nationalist and the founder of the Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910), the first all-India women's organisation; she was a niece of Rabindranath Tagore.

• Manikuntala Sen was a communist leader and author of the memoir "In Search of Freedom" (Shediner Kotha).

NOTE

• "Aamar Jiban" is a landmark text of 19th-century Bengal Renaissance literature and an important source on the social condition of women.

• Related firsts: Savitribai Phule — India's first woman teacher; Kadambini Ganguly and Anandibai Joshi — India's first women doctors.

question: Where is the Vivekanand Rock Memorial situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanyakumari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vivekananda Rock Memorial stands on a small rocky island off the coast of Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, where the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean meet. (विवेकानंद रॉक मेमोरियल — कन्याकुमारी)

• It was built in 1970 to mark the spot where Swami Vivekananda is believed to have meditated in 1892 and attained enlightenment before leaving for the World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago (1893).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The memorial was constructed largely through the efforts of Eknath Ranade and the Vivekananda Kendra.

• Nearby stands the 133-foot statue of the Tamil poet-saint Thiruvalluvar, author of the Thirukkural.

• Kanyakumari is the southernmost tip of mainland India.

NOTE

• Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902), born Narendranath Datta, was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897). His birthday, 12 January, is celebrated as National Youth Day.

question: Under which Act was the rule of British Crown established over India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act 1858.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of India Act, 1858 — also called the Act for the Good Government of India — abolished the East India Company and transferred the powers of government, territories and revenues directly to the British Crown. (भारत शासन अधिनियम 1858)

• It was passed in the wake of the Revolt of 1857.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Key features of the 1858 Act: it created the office of the Secretary of State for India (a member of the British Cabinet) assisted by a 15-member Council of India; it ended the Board of Control and the Court of Directors (i.e., the dual government of Pitt's India Act 1784); and the Governor-General was re-designated Viceroy of India — Lord Canning being the first Viceroy.

• Regulating Act of 1773 — the first step of British Parliamentary control; made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings).

• Charter Act of 1813 — ended the Company's trade monopoly in India (except in tea and trade with China).

• Charter Act of 1833 — made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck) and centralised administration.

NOTE

• The proclamation of Queen Victoria at the Allahabad Durbar (1 November 1858), read by Lord Canning, announced the assumption of Crown rule. Victoria was later declared Empress of India by the Royal Titles Act, 1876.

question: The Kolar region of Karnataka is famous for which mineral from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) in the Kolar district of Karnataka are famous for gold mining. (कोलार — सोना) For decades KGF was India's principal source of gold; the mines were finally closed in 2001.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other gold-bearing areas in India: Hatti (Raichur, Karnataka) — currently the only major working gold mine — and the Ramagiri fields (Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh).

• Coal: mainly from Jharkhand (Jharia, Bokaro), Odisha (Talcher), Chhattisgarh (Korba) and West Bengal (Raniganj).

• Petroleum: Mumbai High (offshore Maharashtra), Digboi (Assam), Ankleshwar (Gujarat).

• Copper: Khetri (Rajasthan), Singhbhum (Jharkhand), Balaghat (Madhya Pradesh).

NOTE

• Karnataka is India's leading producer of gold and is also rich in iron ore (Bellary–Hospet) and manganese. The KGF mines are among the deepest in the world.

question:
Match the following performances of Indian naatya, which were presented by the means of variegated components:

1) Angika          (a) costumes and make-up

2) Vachika        (b) depiction of mental or psychological states

3) Aharya          (c) spoken words

4) Sattvika       (d) gestures and other bodily movements
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-d, 2-c, 3-a, 4-b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni describes four kinds of abhinaya (modes of expression) used in Indian naatya (drama/dance):

◦ Angika abhinaya — expression through gestures and other bodily movements (अंगिक — शरीर की गति) → (d)

◦ Vachika abhinaya — expression through spoken words, song and recitation (वाचिक — वाणी) → (c)

◦ Aharya abhinaya — expression through costumes, make-up, ornaments and stage decor (आहार्य — वेशभूषा) → (a)

◦ Sattvika abhinaya — expression of mental or psychological states, the involuntary emotional response (सात्विक — मनोभाव) → (b)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Natya Shastra (c. 200 BCE – 200 CE) is the oldest surviving treatise on dramaturgy, dance and music, and is often called the fifth Veda (Panchama Veda).

• It expounds the Rasa theory — the eight/nine rasas (sentiments): Shringara, Hasya, Karuna, Raudra, Veera, Bhayanaka, Bibhatsa, Adbhuta and later Shanta.

NOTE

• All eight classical dance forms of India — Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya — draw upon the Natya Shastra's four abhinayas.

question: In Fencing, a contest between the two fencers is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is bout.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In fencing, a bout is the term for a contest/match between two fencers. (तलवारबाज़ी — दो प्रतिद्वंद्वियों के बीच मुक़ाबला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Riposte — an offensive action made immediately after successfully parrying the opponent's attack.

• Parry — a defensive action that deflects the opponent's blade away.

• Remise — a renewed attack made immediately after the first attack is parried, without withdrawing the arm.

• Other fencing terms: piste (the playing strip), en garde (the ready position), touch/touché (a valid hit), lunge, foible and forte.

NOTE

• Fencing has three weapons — foil, épée and sabre — and is one of the few sports that has featured in every modern Olympic Games since 1896.

• The international governing body is the Fédération Internationale d'Escrime (FIE).

question: In which year has the Government of India instituted Arjuna Award to recognise outstanding achievement in national sports events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1961.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arjuna Award was instituted by the Government of India in 1961 to recognise outstanding achievement in national sports. (अर्जुन पुरस्कार — 1961)

• It is conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and consists of a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a scroll of honour and a cash prize.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's sports awards and the years they were instituted:

◦ Arjuna Award — 1961 (consistent outstanding performance over four years).

◦ Dronacharya Award — 1985 (outstanding coaches).

◦ Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award — 1991–92 (the highest sporting honour; earlier called the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna).

◦ Dhyan Chand Award — 2002 (lifetime achievement in sports).

◦ Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar — 2009 (for organisations promoting sports).

• The first Khel Ratna awardee was the chess Grandmaster Viswanathan Anand (1991–92).

NOTE

• National Sports Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of the hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand, and the sports awards are traditionally presented on this day.

question: ‘Atla Taddi’, a festival celebrated by married and unmarried women alike to seek the blessings of Devi Gauri for a long and happy married life and a suitable groom, respectively, is celebrated in ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Atla Taddi" (also written Atla Tadde) is a festival of Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana), observed by women who fast and worship Devi Gauri (Parvati). Married women pray for the long life of their husbands and a happy married life, while unmarried girls pray for a suitable groom. (अटला तद्दी — आंध्र प्रदेश)

• It falls on the third day after the full moon in the month of Ashwayuja (Ashwin), and "atlu" refers to the dosa-like pancakes offered to the goddess.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other major festivals of Andhra Pradesh: Ugadi (the Telugu New Year), Sankranti, Bathukamma (Telangana), Bonalu and the Tirupati Brahmotsavam.

• Similar women's fasting festivals elsewhere: Karva Chauth (North India), Vat Savitri (Maharashtra/UP), Teej (Rajasthan/Bihar) and Chhath (Bihar/Jharkhand/UP).

NOTE

• Andhra Pradesh's capital region is Amaravati; the state is famous for the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, Kuchipudi dance and the Kondapalli toys.

question: PT Usha was elected as the president of which association in December 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Olympic Association.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary athlete P. T. Usha was elected President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) in December 2022. She is the first woman and the first Olympian to head the IOA. (भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ — पी. टी. उषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pilavullakandi Thekkeparambil Usha, from Kerala, is nicknamed the "Payyoli Express" and the "Golden Girl of India".

• At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics she missed a bronze in the 400 m hurdles by 1/100th of a second — the closest an Indian woman had come to an individual Olympic medal at that time.

• She won four golds and one silver at the 1986 Seoul Asian Games, and was honoured with the Padma Shri and the Arjuna Award. She was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 2022.

NOTE

• The Indian Olympic Association, founded in 1927, selects and sends Indian teams to the Olympic Games, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games. Its first president was Sir Dorabji Tata.

question: According to the first Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 report of NITI Aayog, which state stands at the first place in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to NITI Aayog's first National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, released in November 2021, Bihar stood first — that is, it recorded the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor people (about 51.91% of its population) among all States and Union Territories. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2021 — बिहार शीर्ष पर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The order of the poorest States in that report was Bihar (51.91%) > Jharkhand (42.16%) > Uttar Pradesh (37.79%) > Madhya Pradesh (36.65%). Kerala (0.71%) was the least poor, followed by Goa, Sikkim and Tamil Nadu.

• India's national MPI is based on the global MPI of the UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative) and uses 12 indicators grouped under three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living.

• Data source: the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4, 2015-16) for the first report.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister, and it is headed operationally by a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO.

question: What is the full form of UPSC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Public Service Commission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• UPSC stands for the "Union Public Service Commission" — India's central recruiting agency, which conducts the Civil Services Examination and other all-India examinations. (संघ लोक सेवा आयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The UPSC is a constitutional body established under Articles 315 to 323 (Part XIV) of the Constitution of India.

• Its origins lie in the first Public Service Commission set up on 1 October 1926 under the Government of India Act, 1919; it became the Federal Public Service Commission under the Act of 1935 and the UPSC after independence.

• The Chairman and members are appointed by the President and hold office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

• Headquarters: Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi.

NOTE

• The UPSC conducts the Civil Services Exam (IAS/IPS/IFS), CDS, NDA, CAPF, Engineering Services, Combined Medical Services and the Indian Forest Service examinations. Recruitment for Group B and C posts is handled by the SSC (Staff Selection Commission).

question: To which of the state does Sattriya classical dance belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sattriya is the classical dance form of Assam. (सत्रीया — असम) It was introduced in the 15th–16th century by the great Vaishnava saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva as a medium of devotional expression (bhakti) in the monasteries called "sattras", from which the dance takes its name.

• Sattriya was formally recognised as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The eight classical dances of India and their States:

◦ Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu

◦ Kathak — Uttar Pradesh

◦ Kathakali — Kerala

◦ Mohiniyattam — Kerala

◦ Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh

◦ Odissi — Odisha

◦ Manipuri — Manipur

◦ Sattriya — Assam

NOTE

• Sattriya is accompanied by the khol (drum), taal (cymbals) and flute, and performances draw on the Ankiya Naat plays of Sankardeva.

• Folk dances of Assam include Bihu, Bagurumba and Jhumur.

question: Who among the following was a renowned dancer and the first person from Odisha to receive ‘Padma Vibhushan’ in 2000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004), the legendary Odissi dancer and guru, was the first person from Odisha to be awarded the Padma Vibhushan, which he received in 2000. (केलुचरण महापात्र — पद्म विभूषण, 2000)

• He is credited with reviving and codifying Odissi in the 20th century and giving it its present classical form.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He had earlier received the Padma Shri (1972) and the Padma Bhushan (1988), along with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and its Fellowship.

• His famous disciples include Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi, Madhavi Mudgal, Protima Bedi and Kumkum Mohanty.

• Gangadhar Pradhan and Mayadhar Raut were also distinguished Odissi gurus (Mayadhar Raut received the Padma Shri).

NOTE

• Order of civilian honours: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. They were instituted in 1954 and are announced on Republic Day.

• Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha and is associated with the Jagannath temple at Puri and the tradition of the Maharis and Gotipuas.

question: Which musical instrument does N Rajam play?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prof. N. Rajam (Narmada Rajam) is a celebrated Indian violinist of the Hindustani classical tradition. (वायलिन वादिका — एन. राजम)

• She is famous for the "gayaki ang" style — playing the violin so that it imitates the human singing voice — a technique she learnt from Pandit Omkarnath Thakur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri (1984), the Padma Bhushan (2004), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and its Fellowship. She headed the Faculty of Performing Arts at Banaras Hindu University.

• Instrument–exponent pairs frequently asked in SSC:

◦ Sitar — Pandit Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee

◦ Santoor — Pandit Shivkumar Sharma

◦ Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ali Akbar Khan

◦ Shehnai — Ustad Bismillah Khan

◦ Flute (Bansuri) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia

◦ Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha

◦ Violin (Carnatic) — Dr. L. Subramaniam, Lalgudi Jayaraman

NOTE

• The violin is a bowed string (chordophone) instrument of Western origin that was adopted into both Carnatic and Hindustani music; it has four strings and is played with a bow.

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barter system.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The barter system is not a function of money at all — it is the pre-monetary system of exchanging goods directly for goods, which money was invented to replace. (वस्तु विनिमय प्रणाली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The four main functions of money are:

◦ Medium of exchange — money is accepted in payment for goods and services, removing the need for a "double coincidence of wants".

◦ Unit of account (measure of value) — the value of every good is expressed in money terms.

◦ Store of value — purchasing power can be saved for future use.

◦ Standard of deferred payment — future payments (loans, salaries, rents) are stated in money.

• The main defects of the barter system were the lack of a double coincidence of wants, the absence of a common measure of value, the indivisibility of certain goods and the difficulty of storing wealth.

NOTE

• In India, currency notes are issued by the Reserve Bank of India (except the ₹1 note, issued by the Ministry of Finance), and coins are minted by the Government of India. Money supply measures are M1, M2, M3 and M4, with M3 as the "aggregate monetary resources".

question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the population density recorded in Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1106 persons/km².

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Bihar recorded a population density of 1,106 persons per square kilometre, making it the most densely populated State in India. (बिहार — 1106 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Population density = total population ÷ total land area.

• Census 2011 (15th Census) key figures:

◦ India's population — 121.09 crore; density — 382 persons/km².

◦ Most populous State — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim.

◦ Highest density among States — Bihar (1,106), followed by West Bengal (1,028) and Kerala (860); lowest — Arunachal Pradesh (17).

◦ Highest density among UTs — Delhi (11,320); overall sex ratio — 943; literacy rate — 74.04%.

◦ Motto of Census 2011 — "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• The first complete synchronous census of India was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon; the first non-synchronous attempt was in 1872 under Lord Mayo. The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

question: Carbohydrates are utilised by the human body in the form of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is glucose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All digestible carbohydrates (starch, sucrose, lactose, etc.) are broken down in the digestive tract into the simple sugar glucose, which is absorbed into the blood and used by the body's cells as their primary source of energy. (कार्बोहाइड्रेट — ग्लूकोज़ के रूप में)

• Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is oxidised during cellular respiration to release energy stored as ATP.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Amino acids are the digestion products of proteins, not carbohydrates.

• Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

• Fibre (cellulose) is a carbohydrate that the human body cannot digest; it adds roughage and helps bowel movement.

• Excess glucose is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles (and as fat).

NOTE

• Carbohydrates provide about 4 kcal per gram, proteins about 4 kcal/g, and fats about 9 kcal/g.

• Insulin (from the beta cells of the pancreas) lowers blood glucose, while glucagon raises it; their imbalance causes diabetes mellitus.

question: Which Indian musician is associated with the tabla?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zakir Hussain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Zakir Hussain is the world-renowned Indian musician associated with the tabla. (तबला — ज़ाकिर हुसैन) He was the son and disciple of the great tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He received the Padma Shri (1988), the Padma Bhushan (2002) and the Padma Vibhushan (2023), along with multiple Grammy Awards.

• He co-founded the fusion groups Shakti (with John McLaughlin) and Planet Drum (with Mickey Hart).

• Ustad Bismillah Khan — shehnai (Bharat Ratna, 2001).

• Pandit Ravi Shankar — sitar (Bharat Ratna, 1999).

• Ilaiyaraaja — a celebrated South Indian film composer.

NOTE

• The tabla is a pair of drums — the smaller wooden dayan/tabla played with the right hand and the larger metal bayan/dagga played with the left. It is a membranophone.

• Major tabla gharanas: Delhi, Ajrada, Lucknow, Farukhabad, Banaras and Punjab.

question: On whose advice did Gandhiji spend a year travelling around British India to know the people of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On returning from South Africa in January 1915, Mahatma Gandhi travelled across British India for one year on the advice of his political guru, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, in order to understand the country and its people before entering politics. (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले — गांधीजी के राजनीतिक गुरु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866–1915) was a moderate leader of the Indian National Congress, its President in 1905 (Banaras session), and the founder of the Servants of India Society (1905).

• Gandhiji called Gokhale his political guru and wrote about him in his autobiography "The Story of My Experiments with Truth".

• Shrimad Rajchandra, a Jain poet-philosopher, was Gandhiji's spiritual guide.

NOTE

• After this year of travel, Gandhiji founded the Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab/Sabarmati (1915) and launched his first Indian satyagrahas at Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad (1918) and Kheda (1918).

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak called Gokhale the "Diamond of India"; Gandhiji's other mentors included Dadabhai Naoroji, the "Grand Old Man of India".

question: Which deficit indicates the borrowing requirements of the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal deficit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fiscal deficit is the excess of total government expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings. It therefore shows exactly how much the government needs to borrow in a financial year — that is, it indicates the borrowing requirement of the government. (राजकोषीय घाटा — सरकार की उधार आवश्यकता)

◦ Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure – Total Receipts (excluding borrowings)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure – Revenue Receipts. It shows that the government's current earnings fall short of its current spending.

• Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit – Interest Payments. It shows the current year's borrowing need excluding the burden of past debt.

• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit – Grants for the creation of capital assets.

• "Capital deficit" is not a standard budgetary term.

NOTE

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act) sets targets for containing the fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP.

• A high fiscal deficit can be financed by market borrowings, borrowing from the RBI (deficit financing) or disinvestment, and may lead to inflation and a debt trap.

question: Which of the following fundamental duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?
option_1: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
option_2: To protect and to improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures
option_3: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years
option_4: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
solution_text:
The correct answer is To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the eleventh Fundamental Duty — Article 51A(k) — making it the duty of every parent or guardian "to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years". (86वां संविधान संशोधन, 2002)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The same 86th Amendment also:

◦ inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 a Fundamental Right, and

◦ modified Article 45 of the Directive Principles to cover early childhood care and education for children below six years.

• It led to the enactment of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

• The other three options are among the original ten Fundamental Duties added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV-A, Article 51A, of the Constitution and now number eleven. They are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts.

question: Which of the following rocks is formed during the metamorphism of rocks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Slate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Slate is a metamorphic rock. It is formed when the sedimentary rock shale (or clay) is subjected to great heat and pressure deep within the Earth's crust. (स्लेट — कायांतरित चट्टान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Conglomerate and Sandstone are sedimentary rocks, formed by the compaction and cementation of gravel and sand respectively.

• Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock, formed by the rapid cooling of lava at the Earth's surface (the Deccan Traps are made of basalt).

• Important metamorphic transformations:

◦ Shale/Clay → Slate

◦ Limestone → Marble

◦ Sandstone → Quartzite

◦ Granite → Gneiss

◦ Coal → Graphite → Diamond

◦ Basalt → Schist

NOTE

• The three major rock types are igneous (formed from cooled magma/lava), sedimentary (formed from deposited sediments) and metamorphic (formed by heat and pressure acting on existing rocks). Their continuous transformation is called the rock cycle.

• Only sedimentary rocks normally contain fossils.
